newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures drift down but support seen solid.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures drift down but support seen solid.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures tracked sideways to slightly lower over the morning looking for fresh direction but were not expected to move too far from current ranges on Friday, brokers said.
"Some volatility may be caused by the NYMEX products expiry but supports for most contracts are looking fairly solid now so I expect this range will stick for the day," a broker said.
At 1200 GMT the July Brent contract was trading 11 cents down at $19.37 with initial support seen at $19.30 before a solid base around $19.30 down to $18.80 is hit.
Gas oil was off $1 at $173.25 a tonne with $172.25 support.

Nicholas Wilson at MeesPierson said: " The short term target for the July contract is $20.52 with a possible return to $20.60 following the pull back to firm support between the 50 percent retracement mark at $19.20 and the absolute down side at $18.84 which represents the top of the previous trading range".
"The good support at this level could trigger a rally to $20.60 again with medium term target of $21.35, he added.
On gas oil he saw a similar picture though with a slightly more bullish appearance.

"The July market has corrected from the exact 50 percent retracement mark at $172.25. We are now looking for a rally up to $180.50 the recent high with a medium term target at $188.50 and long term $193 contract highs," Wilson said.
